paragraphs.text: Lesson 20, an embarrassing moment. Jim and Fred are at a restaurant, and a waitress comes
to take their order, listen to what happens, and mark these statements true or false.
Welcome to Rudy's Diner, our Super the Days clam chowder, and our specials are Cajun
Chicken and BBQ Ribs. What can I get for you guys?
I'd like this steak, medium rare, with a side of potatoes.
And I'll have the Cajun Chicken with extra hot sauce on the side.
Alright, and anything to drink?
Just tap water for me.
Uh, Diet Coke with no ice.
Coming right up. Nice shirt by the way.
Thank you. That is a nice shirt, Fred. Very trendy.
Thanks. You know the waitress couldn't take her eyes off me? She's pretty cute.
You think I should ask for her number? Couldn't her to try when she comes back with the food?
Yeah. Okay.
So long day at work?
Long week. I thought Friday would never come.
Same here.
Hey, back to your shirt. Is it new?
No. I've had it for years. First time I've worn it though.
Think I got it at a thrift shop. I don't know.
Huh. Cause I've never seen that style of shirt before.
Oh. Now I remember. It was a gift from my Aunt Kay. She's got a knife for fashion.
Yeah. I'd never thought of how cool buttons can look on the back of a shirt.
Cool, but it makes a shirt hard to get into. I couldn't reach you up her button so I'd ask my roommate to give me a hand.
I bet. And that collar. Man. It's very... original.
Yeah. I got a lot of compliments on it at work, but it's kinda uncomfortable. Been tickling my neck all day.
I guess that's the price you pay for being a trendsetter, huh?
Actually, your tag's sticking out. Let me tuck that in for you.
The tag? Oh. That's why it's been bothering me. It's... Hey. Hold on a sec.
Where's a man's room? I'll be right back.
Well, it took you long enough. Had to ask someone for help with the buttons.
Why didn't you just tell me? I feel like an idiot. Where's the fun in that? I wanted to keep dropping hints until you noticed.
Some friend you are. Okay. Here's your steak and potatoes. And here's your cajun chicken.
Hey, your shirt looks much better that way.
Yeah. Enjoy your meal, guys.
Thank you. Smooth. Real smooth. Weren't you going to ask for her number? I can call her back over and ask for some extra napkins.
Forget it. As if she wants to go out with some doofus who put on a shirt backwards.
Oh, man. That was the funniest thing that's happened all week. Easy for you to say. I've never been more embarrassed in my life.
Let's learn the vocabulary from this situation.
The waitress says that the soup of the day is clam chowder.
Clam chowder is a thick soup that contains clams. Clams are a type of shellfish. In a milk or tomato base.
One of the day's specials is cajun chicken.
The adjective cajun refers to a type of cooking from the New Orleans area, which is usually spicy.
The other special is barbecue ribs. Barbecue refers to cooking meat over an open fire.
And ribs are the bones and meat from the animal's side near its heart and lungs.
Jim orders a steak medium rare.
Medium rare means he wants the steak cooked only until a point when it is still pink inside.
If you order a steak rare, that means it will be red inside.
If you order a steak medium, that means it will be fully cooked.
And if you order a steak well done, that means it will be very well cooked.
Fred wants the cajun chicken with extra hot sauce on the side.
In this context, hot means spicy. It doesn't refer to the temperature.
The waitress then asks if they want drinks, and Jim says, just tap water for me.
Tap water is regular water from the faucet, from the sink, not bottled water.
The waitress comments on Fred's shirt, and Jim says that isn't a shirt Fred, very trendy.
Trendy is an adjective, meaning fashionable.
Fred comments, you know the waitress couldn't take her eyes off me.
This expression, she couldn't take her eyes off me, is an informal way to say she continued
to look at me constantly.
Fred wants to ask for the waitress's phone number, and Jim replies, couldn't hurt to try.
This means trying wouldn't have any negative result, so it's a good idea to try.
Fred says it's been a long week at work and that he thought Friday would never come.
Jim replies, same here.
Same here is a quick way to say, I feel the same way, or I'm in the same situation.
Then Jim steers the conversation back to Fred's shirt and asks if it's new.
Fred has had this shirt for years, but it's the first time he's worn it.
At first he thinks he got it at a thrift shop.
A thrift shop is a store that sells used clothing and used items at low prices.
Then Fred remembers that the shirt was actually a present from his Aunt Kay.
He says, she's got an eye for fashion.
If you see someone's got an eye for something, it means they have good taste or good judgment regarding that topic.
Fred had a hard time putting on the shirt, and he had to ask his roommate to give him a hand.
Give someone a hand means to help the person, especially with a physical task.
In response, Jim says, I bet.
I bet means I'm completely sure.
Jim also comments on the collar.
The collar is the part of the shirt that goes around your neck.
Jim says the collar is very original.
In this context, the word original means new and creative, not like anything else.
Fred complains that the collar is a bit uncomfortable.
It's been tickling his neck all day.
The verb tickle means to touch lightly so that it's uncomfortable or provokes laughter.
Jim says, I guess that's the price you pay for being a trendsetter, huh?
The price you pay means the consequences.
It's not talking about an exchange of money, it just means the negative consequences.
A trendsetter is someone who establishes new fashions, usually the first person to use a new trend.
Jim points out that the tag of Fred's shirt is sticking out, and he says, let me tuck that in for you.
The phrasal verb tuck in means put part of some fabric or some clothing inside another part.
We usually use this for your shirt.
Tuck in your shirt means to put the bottom part of your shirt inside your pants.
Fred says, the tag?
Oh, that's why it's been bothering me. It's, hey, hold on a sec.
Hold on a sec means wait a second.
And Jim starts laughing.
Fred asks where the men's room is.
The men's room is another way to say the men's bathroom.
You can say the men's room and the lady's room if you don't want to say the word bathroom directly.
So Fred goes to the men's room and puts his shirt on the proper way.
When he comes back, he says to Jim, why didn't you just tell me I feel like an idiot?
An idiot is a stupid person. It's an insult to call somebody else an idiot.
But Jim preferred to keep dropping hints until Fred noticed.
To drop hints means to suggest indirectly.
Fred says, some friend you are.
That phrase means you're not a very good friend. Fred is speaking sarcastically.
Then the waitress comes and drops off the food.
She says Fred's shirt looks much better now.
After she leaves, Jim says, smooth, real smooth. Weren't you going to ask for her number?
The word smooth can be used as a slang word to say something was well done or done in a socially elegant way.
But here, Jim is speaking sarcastically. In other words, saying that Fred did not behave in a socially elegant way.
Fred doesn't want to ask for the waitress's number anymore because she wouldn't want to go out with some doofus who put his shirt on backwards.
The word doofus is a slang word meaning an incompetent person, someone who is stupid and doesn't know what they're doing.
Jim finds the whole thing very funny, but Fred is quite embarrassed.
That's all the vocabulary from today's conversation.
